description: Make scripts/smoke-redirect.sh safe to point at ANY target (localhost, composed stack, or a deployed CDN-fronted environment) by: (1) deriving the link creation domain from the redirect base URL (or explicit LINK_DOMAIN) instead of hardcoding localhost:3002; (2) creating its own fixtures and cleaning EVERY created link up via a bash EXIT trap so a real environment is left litter-free even on mid-run failure; (3) gating the direct-DB (psql/docker exec) assertions to when DB access is actually available, and adding API-based equivalents so deployed mode still verifies the same facts through the public API/redirect surface; (4) making the three CDN-only assertions (a real slug returns 302 not 404; a country-scoped rule matches; click_events.country is populated) run in ALL modes, with the country-population check done through GET /analytics in deployed mode. Existing local/CI/compose behaviour must be preserved exactly (RD=http://localhost:3002 -> link domain localhost:3002; DATABASE_URL set -> DB checks still run). This is a single coherent rework of one script; keep it dependency-light (bash + curl + node -pe, as today).
steps: Read scripts/smoke-redirect.sh and scripts/integration-assertions.sh in full before editing. Preserve the existing style (ok/bad/expect/contains helpers, loc(), node -pe JSON parsing).

Add a documented env contract to the script header comment: API (default http://localhost:3001/api/v1) and RD (default http://localhost:3002) already exist. Add LINK_DOMAIN: the domain links are created on; default derived from RD by stripping the scheme and any path (so http://localhost:3002 -> localhost:3002, https://snap.example.com -> snap.example.com). Document that LINK_DOMAIN MUST equal the API's DEFAULT_DOMAIN for a freshly-registered workspace (auth.service seeds a system domain == DEFAULT_DOMAIN on register; apps/redirect resolves by matching lower(domains.domain)=normaliseHost(Host), and normaliseHost does NOT strip the port). Document that against a deployed env you set RD to the redirect base URL and API to the API base URL (they may be the same CloudFront host with different paths or different hosts). Document SMOKE_EMAIL/SMOKE_PASSWORD optional overrides in case open registration is disabled (default: self-register a unique throwaway user as today), and note the fallback used when self-register returns no token.

Derive LINK_DOMAIN once near the top: LINK_DOMAIN="${LINK_DOMAIN:-$(printf '%s' "$RD" | sed -E 's#^[a-zA-Z]+://##; s#/.*$##')}". Replace EVERY hardcoded \"domain\":\"localhost:3002\" in the mklink payloads with \"domain\":\"$LINK_DOMAIN\". Confirm that with the default RD this yields the identical byte string localhost:3002 the script uses today (so the compose `integration` job stays green).

Capture created link ids for cleanup: change mklink so that after POST /links it extracts the id from the JSON response (node -pe 'JSON.parse(...).id||""') and appends non-empty ids to a CREATED_IDS array (or newline-accumulated variable). The current script pipes mklink to /dev/null; capture the response into a var first, extract id, then discard. Keep every existing link's slug/behaviour identical.

Add a robust cleanup with a bash EXIT trap installed BEFORE any link is created: trap 'cleanup' EXIT. cleanup() iterates CREATED_IDS and issues DELETE $API/links/$id with the Authorization bearer token (expects 204; ignore errors), so litter is removed even when an assertion fails mid-run or the script is interrupted. Guard against an empty token (skip cleanup with a printed note if registration failed). Do not let cleanup alter the script's overall exit status (preserve the FAILS-based exit code).

Detect DB availability explicitly. Introduce DB_MODE: DB is available when DATABASE_URL is set AND (psql is on PATH OR the snapurl-postgres container is reachable). Wrap the existing dbq-based privacy/city/coordinate/visitor-hash assertions in an `if DB is available` block so they run in local/CI/compose exactly as today, and are SKIPPED (with a printed 'skipped: no DB access (deployed mode)' note, not a FAIL) when no DB is reachable. Do NOT count skips as failures.

Add API-based equivalents that ALWAYS run, so deployed mode still verifies click recording and country population through the public surface. Specifically add a dedicated country-population fixture link with a country routing rule (or reuse the $RUN-geo link), drive a redirect through it with BOTH a non-bot browser User-Agent (copy the BROWSER_UA rationale from integration-assertions.sh -- curl's default UA is classified as a bot and is excluded from the breakdown_daily rollup) AND a CloudFront-Viewer-Country header (e.g. IN), then poll GET "$API/analytics?linkId=<id>&range=24h" with the bearer token until the countries[] breakdown contains the expected country (worker rollup budget: ~90s / matching integration-assertions.sh's 3x30s pattern; parse with node -pe over the JSON body). This verifies 'click_events.country is populated' end-to-end without any DB access. Note in a comment that analytics reads the worker-populated breakdown_daily rollup (apps/analytics.service.ts + apps/worker/src/jobs/rollup.ts), hence the poll budget; and that the API maps country codes to names via COUNTRY_NAMES (IN -> 'India'), so match on either the code or the mapped name as returned.

Ensure the three CDN-only assertions run in ALL modes (they mostly already do via loc()): (a) a real created slug returns 302 with the right Location (existing 'expect "302 to the destination"'); (b) a country-scoped routing rule matches (existing 'India goes to the India store' via CloudFront-Viewer-Country: IN on $RUN-geo); (c) click_events.country is populated -- keep the DB-gated 'CloudFront city header is recorded' check for local/compose AND add the always-run API analytics country-population poll from the previous step. Add a clear section header so it is obvious these three are the deployment showstoppers the issue names.

Keep the final tally + exit code behaviour: [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]. Make sure the EXIT trap's DELETE calls happen but do not clobber that exit code (capture the intended code, run cleanup, then exit with it; or ensure trap runs after the final expression without changing $?).

Run bash -n scripts/smoke-redirect.sh to confirm it parses. Do a dry visual check that with default env the emitted mklink payloads are byte-identical to today's for the domain field (localhost:3002).
acceptance_criteria: With no env overrides, LINK_DOMAIN resolves to localhost:3002 and every mklink payload's domain field equals localhost:3002 (identical to the pre-change script), so the compose `integration` CI job's local path is unaffected.
The script installs an EXIT trap before creating any link, records every created link id, and DELETEs each via $API/links/$id on exit (including on assertion failure), leaving no fixtures behind.

Direct-DB assertions (psql/docker exec: no-ip column, visitor-hash count, city recorded, no-coordinate columns) run only when DATABASE_URL + a reachable DB client/container exist, and are reported as skipped (not failed) otherwise.

An always-run API-based check drives a redirect with a non-bot UA + CloudFront-Viewer-Country header and polls GET /analytics?linkId=...&range=24h until the country appears in countries[], within a ~90s budget, verifying click_events.country population without DB access.
The three CDN-only assertions (real slug 302 not 404; country rule matches; click_events.country populated) are present and execute in every mode.
The script header documents the env contract: API, RD, LINK_DOMAIN (and its DEFAULT_DOMAIN alignment requirement), optional SMOKE_EMAIL/SMOKE_PASSWORD, and how to target a deployed environment.
Final exit code is 0 only when FAILS==0, and cleanup does not corrupt that exit code.
verification: grep -c 'localhost:3002' the emitted domain fields equals the count of mklink calls under default env (visual/manual confirm domains are $LINK_DOMAIN and resolve to localhost:3002 by default)
Confirm a `trap ... EXIT` is installed before the first mklink and a cleanup function issues DELETE $API/links/$id
Confirm the DB-gated block is conditional on DATABASE_URL + client availability and prints a skip note otherwise
Confirm the analytics country poll uses a non-bot UA, a CloudFront-Viewer-Country header, GET /analytics?linkId=...&range=24h, and a ~90s poll budget
pnpm type-check && pnpm test still pass (no app code changed)
findings: Reworked scripts/smoke-redirect.sh into a target-agnostic smoke suite. Changes: (1) Added a full env-contract header comment documenting API, RD, LINK_DOMAIN (with its DEFAULT_DOMAIN + Host-match alignment requirement), optional SMOKE_EMAIL/SMOKE_PASSWORD (login instead of self-register when open registration is disabled), and how to point at a deployed CloudFront env. (2) Derived LINK_DOMAIN="${LINK_DOMAIN:-$(printf '%s' "$RD" | sed -E 's#^[a-zA-Z]+://##; s#/.*$##')}"; verified default RD yields the byte string localhost:3002 and https://snap.example.com/x yields snap.example.com. Replaced all 12 hardcoded "domain":"localhost:3002" mklink payloads with $LINK_DOMAIN (grep confirms 12 uses, 0 hardcoded remaining). (3) mklink now captures the created id from the POST /links JSON (node -pe with try/catch) into CREATED_IDS[]; installed `trap cleanup EXIT` BEFORE the first mklink; cleanup() DELETEs each id via $API/links/$id with the bearer token, guards on empty ACCESS, and preserves the FAILS-based exit code by capturing $? and re-exiting with it (verified with an isolated harness: exit 0 when FAILS=0, exit 1 when FAILS>0, cleanup runs in both). (4) Gated the direct-DB privacy/city/visitor-hash/coordinate assertions behind DB_AVAILABLE (DATABASE_URL set AND (psql reachable via `select 1` OR snapurl-postgres container reachable)); prints a `SKIP` note (new skip() helper, not counted as FAIL) in deployed mode. (5) Added an ALWAYS-RUN API-based country-population check under a new 'deployment showstoppers' section header: drives $RUN-geo with BROWSER_UA (non-bot, copied rationale from integration-assertions.sh) + CloudFront-Viewer-Country: IN, then polls GET /analytics?linkId=<geo id>&range=24h for ~90s until countries[] contains label 'IN' or 'India' (COUNTRY_NAMES mapping). GEO_ID is taken from the last CREATED_IDS entry with an empty-array guard so `set -u` cannot abort the script. (6) The three CDN-only showstoppers are documented and run in all modes: real slug 302 (basic redirect), country rule matches (India store), click_events.country populated (DB-gated city check for local/compose + the always-run analytics poll everywhere). Verification: `bash -n scripts/smoke-redirect.sh` passes; empty/populated CREATED_IDS indexing and empty-array iteration tested under set -uo pipefail; exit-code+trap interaction tested. Node/pnpm are NOT installed in this sandbox so pnpm type-check/test could not be run here, but this change is bash-only and touches no app code, so those results are unaffected; the composed run is validated by the CI `integration` job on the PR (the default local/compose path is preserved byte-for-byte on the domain field). Only scripts/smoke-redirect.sh was modified; no workflow files touched (that is FEAT-002). HARDENING FOLLOW-UP (post-v1-review, addressing two non-blocking review findings; only scripts/smoke-redirect.sh changed): (F1) Removed the implicit geo-link selection. Previously GEO_ID was derived from the LAST entry of CREATED_IDS, an ordering coupling that would silently query the wrong link if fixtures were reordered or another link appended after the geo one. mklink now records the created id in a global LAST_ID (instead of the array's last element), and the $RUN-geo create captures GEO_ID="$LAST_ID" immediately at creation time. IMPORTANT: LAST_ID is a global set in the current shell rather than an echoed value captured via command substitution (GEO_ID=$(mklink ...)) on purpose -- command substitution would run mklink in a subshell, so its CREATED_IDS+= append would be lost and cleanup would regress (the geo link would leak and the count would be 11). mklink still appends every created id to CREATED_IDS, so EXIT-trap cleanup is unchanged and still deletes all 12 fixtures. The poll keeps the empty-id guard (if [ -n "$GEO_ID" ]) so set -u cannot abort and the assertion fails cleanly if the geo link was not created. (F2) Replaced the unconditional `ok "created twelve links"` with a real assertion: EXPECTED_LINKS=12, then ok/bad on ${#CREATED_IDS[@]} == EXPECTED_LINKS. On a mismatch (e.g. bad LINK_DOMAIN / domain-mismatch 400s) it now FAILs with 'expected 12, got N (check LINK_DOMAIN matches DEFAULT_DOMAIN)', counting toward FAILS via the existing bad helper, so the run fails at the real problem rather than only via downstream redirect failures. Preserved: default LINK_DOMAIN still derives to localhost:3002; all 12 fixture slugs/payloads unchanged (grep confirms 12 $LINK_DOMAIN domain fields, 0 hardcoded); EXIT-trap cleanup still DELETEs every created link; FAILS-based exit code preserved; dependency-light (bash + curl + node -pe). Verified: `bash -n scripts/smoke-redirect.sh` exits 0; isolated harness under set -uo pipefail confirmed LAST_ID capture keeps CREATED_IDS intact in the parent shell (count correct), the count assertion fires on mismatch, and the empty-id guard does not abort. Node/pnpm still not runnable in this sandbox; bash-only change, no app code touched, composed run validated by CI integration job on the PR.
